title: phragmanthera cornetii
intro: Phragmanthera cornetii, commonly known as the "cornet orchid mistletoe", is a parasitic plant that obtains its nutrients by attaching itself to the branches of its host tree, typically species of Ficus. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine, particularly in the Philippines, to treat various ailments, including fever, cough, and respiratory issues. The health benefits of Phragmanthera cornetii are attributed to its antiviral, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory properties, which are thought to be due to its therapeutic actions of stimulating the immune system and reducing inflammation. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include alkaloids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, although further research is needed to confirm the specific compounds and their mechanisms of action.
